entries.title: Hillside Forest Fire Front
entries.description: A sloped terrain made of green box “tiles” with scattered tree cylinders where a glowing orange fire front crawls uphill, ignites adjacent trees, leaves behind blackened terrain, and shows rising smoke particles and a progress bar of burned area.
entries.seed: Hillside Forest Fire Front: A sloped terrain made of green box “tiles” with scattered tree cylinders where a glowing orange fire front crawls uphill, ignites adjacent trees, leaves behind blackened terrain, and shows rising smoke particles and a progress bar of burned area.

entries.title: Wind-Driven Grassland Fire
entries.description: A flat grassy plane made of small vertical blades that sway and turn from green to yellow to black as a moving wind vector pushes a flickering fire edge across the field, with tiny embers that detach, drift downwind, and ignite new patches.

entries.title: Canyon Wildfire With Spot Fires
entries.description: A 3D canyon mesh with cliffs and a valley floor where fire particles follow the contours, jump across the canyon via glowing ember particles carried by turbulent updrafts, and create new spot fires that expand and merge, with labels for “primary” and “spot” fires.

entries.title: Urban–Wildland Interface Burn
entries.description: A mixed scene of box “houses” on a grid next to a forest slope, where a forest fire advances toward structures, roofs can ignite and collapse into black debris, and thin water jet objects from fire engines can be steered to cool and turn burning tiles blue.

entries.title: Layered Soil and Root Burn
entries.description: A cutaway terrain block showing surface litter, duff, and mineral soil layers where surface flames crawl over the top while slow-burning red-orange glow spreads underground along semi-transparent root tubes, leaving hollow, collapsing soil pockets.

entries.title: Mountain Ridge Fire and Shadowed Slopes
entries.description: A ridged terrain surface where sunlit slopes warm and turn more flammable (color-shifting toward yellow-red) while shaded slopes stay moist (blue-green), and the fire front wraps around the ridge, accelerates on hot aspects, and stalls or shrinks on cooler sides.

entries.title: Crown Fire in a Conifer Stand
entries.description: A row of tall cone-shaped trees where fire climbs trunks, then leaps into the crowns, creating a fast-moving canopy fire that sends bright ember particles upward, with the ground fire moving slower below and a vertical profile showing heat intensity versus height.

entries.title: Patchy Fuel Mosaic Fire
entries.description: A large grid of terrain cells with different fuel types (grass, shrubs, bare rock) color-coded, where fire spreads quickly through some cells, skips over rock gaps, and occasionally backtracks via glowing ember particles that land in isolated fuel patches.

entries.title: Firebreak and Backburn Operation
entries.description: A forest terrain with a clear-cut firebreak line where the main fire advances, and a controllable backburn line ignites along the break, spreads in the opposite direction, then collides and merges with the main fire, reducing its intensity and changing smoke color.

entries.title: Nighttime Fire Glow and Heat Plume
entries.description: A gently rolling terrain with dim ambient light where the fire perimeter glows bright orange, a semi-transparent rising plume shows heat as a colored vertical volume, and tiny spark particles drift upward and fade, with a side thermometer bar tracking maximum plume height.

entries.description: A rugged terrain with protruding rock blocks and narrow gullies where fire skirts around nonflammable rock columns, funnels and accelerates through gullies, and occasionally sends sparks up to ignite vegetation on top of isolated rocky plateaus.
